description: We are a group of Developers, AI Engineers and Designers.
summary: Cabin Playground helps the people who design spacecraft cabins, rovers and Moon or Mars bases work with NASA's microgravity fire data. You set the cabin's oxygen and pressure, put everyday items into a 3D ISS Destiny module, and see what NASA's PSI fire experiments recorded for each item under Prevent, Detect and Suppress. It covers 655 test rows from BASS, BASS-II, Saffire I to III, SAME, SAME-R and FLEX. Each finding links back to the exact NASA record it came from. The app also shows where the evidence stops. Every gap says why it's blank and names the test that would close it, for example "PMMA at 34% O₂, 8.2 psi, 0.16 g". This matters because NASA's fire data is spread across tables, test matrices and papers, and nothing tells a designer which test fits their cabin or what has never been tested. Learning that early in a design costs far less than learning it in orbit.
details:
What it does: a cabin designer picks a preset (ISS, Rover, Moon base) or sets oxygen and pressure, then drags items such as cotton, acrylic, wiring, foam and fuels into a 3D cabin. Each item gets a live closeness tag against the PSI data: Tested near these conditions, O₂ match (pressure not stated), Not tested here, or Not recorded. Clicking Start investigation sorts the cabin's records by defense. Prevent asks whether it will ignite and spread. Detect asks what smoke a detector would see. Suppress asks what puts the flame out. Items NASA saw burn near your conditions catch fire in the 3D scene.

How it works: a Python pipeline downloads the PSI CSVs, checks each file's SHA-256 and joins every table to its as-run test matrix, readme and reports. That turns outcomes into statements like "went out when the airflow was cut" instead of a bare yes or no. Seven evidence packets add measured series: FLEX droplet diameters, BASS flame height measured from video, and Saffire publication findings, each viewable as a chart. A Claude agent investigates the cabin through 10 typed tools that query the records. Deterministic code runs every query and computes every "Test next" condition. The model writes neither.

Benefits and impact: designers find out early which materials have evidence at their atmosphere and which don't. For example, acrylic has 177 NASA burn tests and none is near a 34% O₂ Moon cabin. Researchers get a list of concrete experiments that would fill real gaps.

Design factors: we show the record, not a verdict. There are no safety scores or risk rankings. Unknown values stay "not stated" with a reason, and outcomes are never borrowed between materials. Gravity is a standing gap, because every PSI test flew in microgravity. Users bring their own API key in Settings.

Tools: TypeScript, Next.js 15, React 19, React Three Fiber and three.js, Zustand, Zod, Tailwind, the Anthropic SDK, Python, Blender, and Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext.

What's creative: it turns a scattered archive into a cabin you can walk through, and it treats the gaps as the product, so every blank becomes a proposed experiment.
